answer.evidence: This is a car shown from the side (red tail light on the left, yellow headlight on the right), so it is not really box-like. The roof is a light panel in rows 6-16 that ends in a darker edge line at row 16, and the hood and trunk are light deck panels in rows 13-24 that end in a gray edge line at row 24. Together these read as horizontal surfaces seen from above, about 12 rows tall. Below them the door and body side is a vertical south face in rows 25-41 (about 17 rows) with wheels under it. Because it has both top surfaces and a front face of 3+ rows, it reads as three_quarter, though the top surfaces are somewhat ambiguous.

styleAnswer.evidence: The white car has a near-neutral dark outline: 89% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, against 0-1% for the hedge and cheese stall, which carry tinted outlines. The body is mostly white and light grey, about 3 steps, with one flat panel shade and little grain. The windows are flat blue-grey fills, and the wheels are dark discs with a light hub and no tonal grading. Visible tones per tile (9) match the hedge, but the stall (17) and well (20) are clearly richer. Flat coverage is 14%, in line with the stall (13%), but the large body panels read as flat fills with no speckle, dirt, panel-edge highlight or tile-like texture. Overall it looks like a clean sticker next to the references, which have material-toned outlines and multi-step shading.
